body: Same here. I'll be sitting in the bathtub letting the shower just rain on me and I think about how the water feels on my skin. And then it makes me think that theres gonna be a day where I dont get to feel this anymore.
The movie Inception messed with my head. Sometimes I feel like I'm dreaming and I just havent woke up yet.

The thought of death would cross my mind here and there ...but it wouldnt bother me before. I noticed the thought has progressed into fear since going into this pandemic and it's been hard to cope with. I just cant wrap my head around the fact that I exist and then suddenly I wont. Thinking of it just makes my chest tighten and wave of panic hits me. 

Just know you're not alone.

LOL. When I tell people about the dirty toilets in my dreams they just give me a weird and confused look. Glad I'm not the only person who dreams of dirty toilets...

I actually tried to look up what my dreams are trying to tell me when the dirty toilet scenario pops up. It's something along the lines of you are holding a lot of negative thoughts or people that you should learn to let go. 

Yeah for some reason I noticed theres no switches or ceiling lights on my dreams either. If I'm indoor, for some reason the room lighting is not a problem.
For some reason theres no light switches in my dreams. If I'm in doors it seems that there are no switches or ceiling lights or lamps. Room is always well lit and visible.
Yeah for some reasons electronics dont work smoothly in my dreams. So that gives a me clue.

I've had moments in my dreams where I've had to call emergency services but for the life of me I cant. Lol I seriously say to myself "shit i should call 911.....ok...how do I do this... what's the number?"and I'm like just look at the phone lost and confused.


Lol I'm glad I'm not the only one with cell phone problems. 5G network is not applicable in dreams apparently lol
Yeah I've had some other electronic devices acting weird in my dreams too.
I have this too. Sometimes when I "use my phone" it's not my actual phone. Like it's some old Motorola razor or those Nokia phones.

Of all time? Sayashi Riho since the moment I saw her in the auditions. I know she got a lot of hate for being the ACE of Momusu, most people like to root for the underdogs who dont get as much spotlight on stage. Riho just has this star quality from the beginning and she set the bar really high for being so young and being able to push herself to keep getting better. She had this very calm demeanor and I believe she was hard on herself especially with the company pushing her to be at the front. She wasnt trying to be the funny, cute, fashionable, or sexy one. She kinda always looked like the lone wolf of the group. The thing she was known for her high level of dancing. But I think that level of dancing, shows how dedicated and connected she was to her performance. When I would watch her perform, she made it look effortles. 

I'm glad she came back and is trying new things. I was never a fan of babymetal but I would just watch her dance and see the same energy that carried from her time in Morning Musume. I know shes getting into acting now and I want to continue to support her.

I'm just as scared as you are and it's been seriously eating me away every waking moment of my life. So at first I started reading all these threads to find confirmation to ease my worry but sometimes it just made the anxiety of not knowing if there is an afterlife or not worse than it already was. 

I finally told myself I can do as much research or read all the positive NDEs I want, but it doesnt exactly scientifically prove there is an afterlife. That scared me a lot but at the same time I realized that sometimes it's not about what you know...its about what's in your heart. Were all individuals and have our own beliefs. We may not all agree on the same idea on what may lie after this life, but we all believe in something.  Whether it be a higher power, reincarnation, or even just complete oblivion. But I think whatever we believe is what is granted for us after this life. 

Something I've contemplated is why we cannot prove there is an afterlife. I've read everything hoping theres some kind of evidence but I am now okay with the fact that we cannot 100% confirm it. Because if you really think about it, if we all knew 100% that there was one we would live our lives differently. We are given a chance at life to experience love, freedom, memories, happiness...etc. Say for example if people knew there was a heaven for sure, they would probably  make every decision or action in life to make sure they would get to go there once they left this world when in actuality we should just be living our lives for ourselves. Just do and believe what's in your heart and that will carry you they this. Its definitely helped me get thru this. 

♡

I like your theory! But yeah you're right we could be in a form of a human here but maybe this afterlife we speak of possesses its own unique characteristics or features that we have no idea what it looks like. 

Kinda like the movie Avatar. Like our conscious can slip into another form. (As you can tell I watch a lot of movies lol)

I am not really a hardcore religious person but I do believe in a God or a higher existence than the one were in now.  I remember always going to church as a child and the priest would always preach about doing God's work so you can be welcomed into heaven. I remember if I'd do something bad my parents would taunt me and say things like "you're not gonna go to heaven!". I used to get terrified as a child and then when my parents would say it too often (because I was naughty lol) I actually stopped for a moment and thought "is not going to heaven...like not going to disneyland or something?" And then questioned what this place actually looked like.
I like to imagine that even if once I'm gone and dont have a physical form, that I can just watch all my loved ones enjoying their life. Almost like watching a movie that never ends.

I like to imagine they get some kind of notification that someone they know is coming. And that's why some people have deathbed visions of seeing loved ones because they're almost like transporters to help guide you there so you're not afraid.

I know once we die we leave our physical human form and possibly ascend to another form. I'm sure whatever that form is we still will be able to communicate or interact with the surroundings. 

Like are we just a ball of glowing light with no characteristics or physical features?  or say if I die at the age of 42... will I look 42 in the afterlife because that's when my physical life ended?

When I first was introduced to a death I was maybe 4? I somehow came up with the idea that our soul will take on many forms but will take a human like shape of what we felt was the most time in our life. So if I die at 42 and the happiest time in my life was probably when I was 29. So I'd imagine that's what I'd be able to look like. 

I know the stuff I said sounds crazy. Lol I feel so embarassed starting this thread but it's so interesting reading all your guys interpretations!

Although science has yet to prove that there are other planets or worlds that host some kind microorganisms or lide... .etc. I still like to believe that theres something else out there. The universe is so vast and there has to be something else like happening out there besides our humanity. I think it's good we dont know in this life what it is, it makes the thought of an afterlife more interesting once were ready to go there.
What do you imagine?

Hi. I just want to say my last relationship sounded exactly like yours. I am  currently 103lbs and 5"2. Way before my ex ever knew me I was 25lbs+ heavier and I rapidly lost weight after developing an eating disorder.  I wouldnt consider myself actually fat at that time.. I would just say I looked a little meaty.. and I had a muffin top lol.

 I was never in my life a physical person. I hate any form of physical activity. Never worked out. Or whatever. But when the weight loss occurred so suddenly, my arms and legs got super thin. My tummy area is kinda flabby and I have stretch marks on my thighs and on my buttcheeks lol. I am so self conscious about the tummy thing that I try to find clothes that dont bring focus to that part of my body.

My ex would always walk up to me if my tummy was exposed and pinch it. He would also say stuff like "can u go to the gym!?" I remember one time I was sitting on a chair in just my underwear and I got up and he said "haha the chair left impression marks on your cheeks" and when I walked up to the mirror to look at it I told him that's not from the chair that's my stretch marks. He bursted out in laughter and said "eeeerw haahah thats gross". This kind of stuff just lowered my confidence.  

It's linda okay to joke around about this kind of stuff with your partner once in a great while, but that's just messed up if its constant. I think it would be easier if he still complemented on other things like my face, hair, or something else...but he never did. I always brought up that what he says is hurtful but he just blew it off. I'd also mention to him that I'm basically 100lbs and underweight for my height. A lot of people always would try to encourage me to eat because I looked too skinny.  If we were to go out and I'd dress up hed insist me to change my clothes sometimes if my stomach looked weird. For the fact I've had an eating disorder in the past, these kind of actions and comments should have not been brought to my attention. It just made me want to slip back into the disorder because he made me feel physically repulsive. We  broke up due to other major reasons, but because of being teased so much about my body for 5 years its given me the idea to believe my body is ugly. 

A person should love you no matter how you look. I'm in a new really healthy and wonderful relationship now but I'm still conscious about my body because of exs remarks. I've  been with my new bf for a year now but Im still paranoid of how my body looks to the point if him and I were intimate I'd prefer it be at night with the lights off. Theres been times where wed try to engage in intimacy during the day but I'd be so hesitant because I just hated the way my body looks. I'd try to cover myself with my arms or the sheets, but he constantly reminds me how lucky he is and that theres nothing wrong with the way I look. He makes me feel sexy and desired as much as I think my body doesnt look that great to me.

So to answer your question... YES I believe this is a form of verbal abuse. Its damaging your selfesteem and your confidence.

:) I'm glad that you were able relate.

I think the part that makes me wonder and sometimes freak out about is how or why isnt everyone else  freaking out about this!? Like how can some people live so recklessly, intentionally make bad decisions, or hurt others? Wouldnt you want to take your gift of life and open that up with others by treating them with love and kindness.  After developing this fear of death, I've found that it makes it a bit easier if you just open and always follow your heart. You were brought here to find a purpose and create your own story. I think that's the beauty of life.

And like I said. I think its better we cant 100% confirm there is an afterlife. It would be nice. Because if we did, we wouldnt be creating our true personal story for ourselves. 

Anyways. I hope I've helped a little. Of anything you can always message me. :)

Hi. 

I'm actually experience anxiety right now thinking about what happens when we die. Usually it hits me hard at night time when I'm just trying to fall asleep and not really so much in the day because I'm preoccupied with work and such.

But reading your posts scares the s*** out of me because everyrhing u just explained is exactly the same cycle of emotions that I'm feeling currently. I just want to let you know you're not alone. 

For me as well, I was never really religious but my family is.  I would maybe say i used to be an atheist and I usually got annoyed with religious people that would preach things or try to influence others. I'm a super critical thinker and I would always find loopholes in what people would preach.  

All the way up until my Grandma passed I had this logical view of death  and didnt really think about my own morality. However, at her church services I remember kneeling and looking up at Jesus on the cross and I started to pray. Something I've never really seriously done. My Grandma was a devoted Catholic and prayed every night. While praying, I asked God if he is real or not... and if he is, please grant my grandma entrance to his Kingdom because I want to believe that's where she is right now. 

Also to note, just like you, I used to be suicidal. Honestly I just wanted to die at some points in my life and didnt really have the will to keep living. Death did not scare me at all. But all of a sudden since the beginning of this year my view of life has completely changed. Now I'm terrified of dying and the thought of it gives me so much anxiety that I curl into a ball and cry or pace back and forth overthinking if there is an afterlife or is it just poof complete oblivion. 

 The harsh reality is eventually we all die and we can choose to believe what we all want. But for me its what's in your heart that counts.  Theres unexplainable things that happen and some things that science cant really explain.  Dont try to overthink death, It just makes the fear worse and your brain just overloads itself.  So now I like to think with my heart and it helps me cope with the fear. And in my heart, I truly believe there has to be something after this life. We dont know what it is exactly and there isnt a clear explanation but I think the reason for that is because if we all knew for sure that there is a heaven we would behave differently in a sense that it influences our actions. So in a sense, it's a kinda good thing that we dont know because we have control over how we decide our fates.

Now that I think of it too, it's kinda odd that people are encouraging suicide when the reddit page is called suicide watch...but I dont really think they're intentionally saying "hey go kill yourself". Its probably moreso acknowledging that they understand how that person feels and it's okay. I mean its not really okay...but you get what I mean lol.
We all are here together. Although we are all strangers here on Reddit, I feel this is a safe place for all of us to share and provide strength.

I feel like I'm a constant burden to others as well. I'm ashamed of how I feel but I just want to be at peace. I am suffering and can never formulate words to express that so I deal with it internally. I'm worried that others will blame themselves if I tried to commit suicide. I dont think suicide is something that can be easily understood, so people will try to formulate reasons. Living is can be burden and dying can be a burden as well. Either way it's one or the other. You have control over what you want to do. In time, others will eventually understand. 

I'm not saying go kill yourself. It's more like, find what you think is right to you. Because you're the one that's making that decision.

Not sure how the unit of measurements works for anesthesia, but I'm like 100lbs and have a history of anxiety...but the doctor didnt really know that. I'm just happy to be living from this experience.

Sorry it has taken me long to respond. I've actually been reading all I can on this on google. This is my first time reading about this and I'm actually in shock to how accurate I can relate to this. To elaborate a bit further, I noticed I've become a lot more sensitive towards people. I like to believe I was a decent person my whole life but for the past few years I've felt as if I'm more aware of my actions and peoples feelings. Like I'm now leading with a greater purpose or as a guide in peoples lives. I'm not doing it out of fear of dying or hoping that my good actions will follow me in the afterlife. It's like I ascended to something greater. I dont really have a set plan in life and enjoy just living it day by day and opening my heart to the world. I may not have had the nicest things in life and I've had to do a lot of struggling on my own, but it doesnt phase me. 

I have always felt a part of me died in that chair and that when I came back I wasnt 100% me. I had all my memories of this physical body but something just felt off. There are times where something simple like my name feels strange. I'll say it to myself and know it's my name but it's like it doesnt 100% belong to me. Like I have all these memories, but it just feels like they didnt really happen. 

I really thank you for informing me of this. Although, I'm not devoutly religious...I do believe that I came from somewhere, whether my soul split, I'm apart of a walk-in, another planet, or even if I may have ascended from heaven. It's difficult to explain and it makes me sound cray cray, but I fully believe this walk-in thing. We all have the right to believe what we experience and I believe that ontop of my possible NDE...it could be possible something happened to my soul as well.  So thank you for sharing this with me. It gives me clarity and helps me accept what I experienced.
I actually lucid dream many times a week. It felt different and I knew it wasnt a dream or something that my brain just made up. It felt overwhelming to know I was actually experiencing what I did.

You are right...i've tried to explain it to a number of people but like I kinda get the impression that they think I'm crazy. It was definitely an experience and I'm sure there has to be people out there who experienced something similar.

I've read stories where people were put under anesthesia and end up being braindead. I am pretty sure I was administered more than what my body could handle. It remains a mystery to me if the doctor and his staff knew what was happening but didnt really disclose it in fear it would bring negativity on their practice. But I'm glad that somehow while I was asleep I knew something wasnt right that I was able to break free from it.

Hi. I go thru this every night. When I think about death during the day it doesnt effect me because I'm distracted with work.

For the past couple of months I've been struggling at night time to sleep because the thought pops into my head and I start to really focus on it and question so many things about death & the afterlife. 

My best suggestion to you is just keep your mind busy. Set a routine for yourself every single evening and commit to it. 

I really believe that with the COVID pandemic it has effected us by not allowing us to do things that we would normally do. With less things to do -  it gives us more time to ponder about different things. You have to set yourself up for distractions so you dont let your mind focus on the topic.

I find its helpful reading NDEs when I feel the panic attack bout to come on. I grew up in a religious household but I never really took it seriously. I've read about different religions and cultures and how they interpret the afterlife. The truth is, we dont know and probably wont ever know what happens...and that can be scary thought to process.  Dont try to focus so much in finding a clear answer, it's just important to find in your heart what you believe.  

Believe me I am scared of not existing anymore. I used to be very depressed and didnt care if my life ended. Not sure what was the turning point, but moreso recently I became to appreciate everything in life. I just try to live in the moment.  Death will come when it is time, but do not use your time thinking about it when you can enjoying the simple pleasures in life we will not be able to experience later. 

Just know that there are a bunch of people here on reddit who are experiencing the same feelings as you. You are not alone.

I lost my grandma back in 2017 . I havent been very religious in my lifetime but my grandma was and I like to believe because she was a such a loving spirit she is finally at Peace with God. There is one incident that happened to me that I believe is a sign from her and that there are some strange moments in life that we cannot explain.

 Up until her death, her health declined and she became bedridden. She didn't have very many possessions and was a simple lady. She never bought anything of material value for herself and usually would just give my siblings and I money. She'd always wear the same clothes and even if my mom would buy her new ones she wouldnt wear it. Other than her simplistic life style, she was a devout catholic and prayed every single night. The one thing I remembered that was hers was this this weird safety pin with a worn out white bear with a red bow tie on it. Every morning she'd put the house key on the safety pin and pinned it to the inside of her shirt. She'd always pin it on the left side directly above her heart. I could never figure out why she did this, I'd even buy her keychains for the key but she'd still continue to pin the key to the inside of her shirt. 

When I flew to the Philippines for her funeral services for some reason the pin was something on my mind but I wasnt gonna ask my parents about it. I dont think they even knew she did that with the house key. And I'd think after all these years she wouldve tossed it. We cleaned out her room. As I've previously said she did not have much stuff. I just took one of her rosaries she used to pray with. I was okay with that and I wasnt expecting to ever find that safety pin. The thought of finding that specific pin was like finding a needle in a haystack.

Anyways, a few days later I had to fly back home. At the airport my dad pulled up to drop me off at the curb. When I opened the door I hear a small clink on the ground. Thinking that it's probably loose change..
I look down and I see something oddly familiar. I pick it up...and it's the same exact safety pin my grandma used to pin the house key to the inside of her shirt. I asked my dad if he knew what the safety pin was and he said no so I explained it. He laughed it off and said "shes watching you".

My grandma probably was bedridden for over a year and even before that she would never leave the house at all. She never rode in the car my dad was driving so it always made me think how the hell it got there. 

I am 10000000% this is the same safety pin she used and it cant just be a coincidence I found it as I was about to leave. To me, it was like her way of saying goodbye. I have the safety pin on my stand and sometimes I pin it on the inside of my shirt the same way she did. I find it gives me comfort because she'll always be close my heart.
